dates.notes: Signed at the Shanghai ceremony on 16 July 2026; open for signature from 1 May to 31 July 2026. The official Chinese text was published by the National People's Congress on 18 November 2026 and its articles were read for this record. China's NPC Standing Committee approved ratification on 6 November 2026; that is a domestic authorisation, not a deposit. No instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession was verified with the depositary, and no depositary notification of entry into force was located. Russia's Government accepted the Agreement by decree No. 1532 of 17 November 2026, published on the official legal-information portal on 18 November 2026; that is also a domestic act, and no Russian deposit was verified.

gaps: Entry into force is not confirmed: Article 15 requires three deposited ratifications, acceptances or approvals, and no deposit was verified. The number of deposits is unknown, not zero. China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026 and Russia's Government accepted the Agreement by decree No. 1532 of 17 November 2026; both are domestic acts. No Chinese or Russian deposit, and no depositary notification, was verified.
China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026. That is a domestic authorisation; the deposit of the instrument and any depositary notification were not verified.

The MFA reports 38 founding members while the signing records individually identify 37; the 38th member is not named in the official sources located. The NDRC repeated the 38 figure on 3 November 2026 without naming the 38th. Bangladesh is not the 38th member: it announced on 1 August 2026 that it would join 'initially as an observer'.
Observer status is not a party status: Article 11 allows the Council to admit non-member States and intergovernmental organisations as observers. No Council admission of Bangladesh is recorded.
No public depositary register or status table for signatures, ratifications and accessions was located; Article 18 designates China as depositary.
The Organization's functions are limited to the civilian domain; military AI is outside the Agreement.

Articles 5–8 provide for a Council, a Secretariat and financing. No evidence was located that the Council or Secretariat has been constituted, that rules of procedure or a budget have been adopted, or that implementing instruments exist. On 3 November 2026 the NDRC said China is advancing the organization's 'material operation' process ('正在推动世界人工智能合作组织的实体化运行进程'), wording that describes work in progress rather than constituted organs. This is an unverified point, not a finding that the organs do not exist.
No deposited or certified copy was acquired; the stored text is the official NPC Chinese publication. The English reproduction on Digital Watch was consulted but is not stored.

legal_nature.rationale: The instrument is a constituent treaty: it establishes an intergovernmental organisation with legal personality (Article 1), provides for signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession (Article 14), entry into force on the third instrument (Article 15) and a depositary (Article 18).

ratifications.note: China is the depositary and no public depositary register or notification was located. No deposited instrument was verified, but the total is unknown rather than zero.

parties.summary: 38 founding members reported by China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; 37 individually identified in the signing records: 29 States at the 16 July 2026 ceremony and eight later signatories named on 30-31 July 2026. The October 2026 progress report says nine States joined after the initial 29, so one of the nine remains unnamed. Bangladesh announced on 1 August 2026 that it would join 'initially as an observer', not as a founding member; no Council admission is recorded. Singapore's MDDI told Parliament on 9 September 2026 that Singapore had received an invitation and would consider it; it is not a member and has not accepted. China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026 and Russia's Government accepted the Agreement by decree No. 1532 of 17 November 2026, but both are domestic acts and no deposit was verified; the number of deposited instruments is unknown.
unknowns: The MFA reports 38 founding members as of 9 November 2026, but the signing records individually identify 37. The October 2026 progress report says nine States joined after the initial 29; eight are named in the 31 July account, so one of the nine - the 38th member - is not named. Bangladesh is not that member: it announced on 1 August 2026 that it would join 'initially as an observer'. Singapore's MDDI told Parliament on 9 September 2026 that Singapore had received an invitation and would consider it, without saying whether the invitation is to membership or observer status; Singapore is not a member and has not accepted.

China is the depositary under Article 18. No public depositary register, status table or notification of signatures, ratifications, acceptances, approvals, accessions or entry into force was located. The number of deposited instruments is therefore unknown; zero deposits are individually verified, but that is not a verified total of zero.
China's NPC approval of 6 November 2026 and Russia's Government acceptance of 17 November 2026 are domestic acts. The date of any deposit, and the treaty's entry into force, were not verified.
The Agreement remains open to accession after 31 July 2026 (Article 14(3)); later accessions are not Founding Members and are not included in this list.
The exact date on which the MFA's 38-country count was reached is not stated; the October 2026 progress report already gives 38.

No act constituting the Council or the Secretariat, appointing a Secretary-General, adopting rules of procedure or a budget, or opening a secretariat in Shanghai was located. The NDRC described 'material operation' as a process under way on 3 November 2026, not as completed.

provenance.discovered_via: CSIS 2026 analysis of global AI governance cited WAICO; the record was opened after the official MFA signing and ratification sources were located.

related.note: China's 2023 Global AI Governance Initiative is the policy line that led to the proposal for WAICO; it is a unilateral non-binding document, whereas the WAICO Agreement is a treaty.
The other AI-specific treaty in the corpus. CETS 225 is a human-rights framework convention; WAICO is a constituent instrument of an intergovernmental organization. Neither is in force.
The US-led Pax Silica coalition is the counterpart architecture. Kazakhstan is a signatory of both the Pax Silica Declaration and the WAICO Agreement.

ai_provisions: Article 1 — establishes WAICO as an independent intergovernmental international organization with international legal personality
Article 2 — purposes: human-centric AI, international cooperation, bridging the AI divide, risk mitigation and trustworthy AI

Article 3 — functions, including capacity building, alignment of governance rules and technical standards, open-source cooperation and support for the UN framework; functions are limited exclusively to the civilian domain
Article 4 — principles: UN Charter, sovereignty, diversity of civilizations, equality, multilateralism and extensive consultation
Articles 5–8 — Council, decision-making, Secretariat and financing
Article 10 — membership open to all States; Founding Members are States that sign during the open-for-signature period

Article 11 — observer status for non-member States and intergovernmental organisations, subject to an application to the Secretariat and approval by the Council; observers may attend the plenary on invitation and have no vote
Article 14 — signature from 1 May to 31 July 2026; ratification, acceptance or approval; accession thereafter
Article 15 — entry into force on the third instrument of ratification, acceptance or approval
Article 18 — China as depositary; Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts equally authentic
relevance.excluded_scope: Military AI is excluded: Article 3(2) limits the Organization's functions exclusively to the civilian domain. The Agreement establishes an organization and a cooperation framework; it does not itself set product rules, prohibitions, testing standards or a judicial dispute-settlement mechanism. Disputes are to be settled by consultation (Article 13).
relevance.reason: The constituent treaty of the first intergovernmental international organization specifically dedicated to artificial intelligence. It establishes WAICO as an independent intergovernmental organization with international legal personality, headquartered in Shanghai, with a Council and a Secretariat, and limits its functions exclusively to the civilian domain of AI (Article 3(2)). It is subject to ratification, acceptance or approval and enters into force on the deposit of the third such instrument (Article 15). It is a treaty, not a political declaration, and it is the second AI-specific treaty in the corpus alongside CETS 225. The article references were checked against the official Chinese text published by the National People's Congress.

status_note: Treaty, binding on States that become parties, but entry into force is not confirmed as of 26 November 2026. Article 15 requires three instruments of ratification, acceptance or approval. China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026 and Russia's Government accepted the Agreement by decree No. 1532 of 17 November 2026; both are domestic acts, recorded separately from international consent, and no deposited instrument was verified. The number of deposits is unknown, not zero: China is the depositary under Article 18 and no public depositary register or notification was located. China's MFA reports 38 founding members, but the signing records individually identify 37: 29 States at the 16 July 2026 ceremony and eight later signatories named on 30-31 July 2026. The October 2026 progress report says nine States joined after the initial 29; eight are named, so one of the nine remains unnamed. On 3 November 2026 the NDRC said China is advancing WAICO's 'material operation' process, wording that describes work in progress rather than constituted organs. Bangladesh announced on 1 August 2026 that it would join 'initially as an observer'; Article 11 requires an observer application and Council approval, and no admission is recorded. Singapore's Ministry of Digital Development and Information told Parliament on 9 September 2026 that Singapore had received an invitation and would consider it; the reply does not say whether the invitation is to membership or observer status, and Singapore has not accepted. The 37/38 discrepancy is recorded, not resolved.
